paragraphs.title: Azariah's Prophecy and the Need to Seek the Lord

easy.explanation: The verse says that the Spirit of God came upon Azariah the son of Oded.
easy.q: Upon whom did the Spirit of God come?

easy.explanation: Azariah went out to meet Asa and spoke to him, Judah, and Benjamin.
easy.q: Whom did Azariah go out to meet?

easy.explanation: Azariah said, “if ye forsake him, he will forsake you.”
easy.q: What will happen if people forsake the Lord?

medium.explanation: The Lord is with His people while they are with Him and seek Him.
medium.q: What condition is given for the Lord to be with His people?

answers: The true God, a teaching priest, and law
A king, a temple, and sacrifices
medium.explanation: Israel had been without the true God, a teaching priest, and law.
medium.q: What does the passage say Israel had been without during a long season?

medium.explanation: “Vexations” refers to troubles, distress, and hardships among the inhabitants.
medium.q: What does the word “vexations” mean in this passage?

answers: Seeking the Lord leads to finding Him, while forsaking Him leads to His forsaking them
challenge.explanation: Azariah connects the people's response to the Lord with the Lord's response to them.
challenge.q: What cause-and-effect relationship does Azariah describe?

answers: All the people went up to Jerusalem
Nation was destroyed by nation and city by city
challenge.explanation: The passage says that nation was destroyed of nation and city of city.
challenge.q: What happened when there was no peace to those going out or coming in?

answers: Because his work would be rewarded
Because there were no more enemies
Because the high places had already been removed
challenge.explanation: Azariah told him, “your work shall be rewarded.”
challenge.q: Why did Azariah encourage Asa to be strong?

paragraphs.title: Religious Reform and the Gathering of the People

easy.explanation: When Asa heard the words and the prophecy, he took courage.
easy.q: How did Asa respond to the prophecy?

easy.explanation: Asa put away the abominable idols from the land.
easy.q: What did Asa put away from the land of Judah and Benjamin?

easy.explanation: They gathered themselves together at Jerusalem.

medium.explanation: Asa renewed the altar of the Lord that was before the porch of the Lord.
medium.q: What did Asa do to the altar of the Lord?

answers: They saw that the Lord his God was with him
They wanted to build another altar
They were commanded to go to war
medium.explanation: They joined Asa in abundance when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.
medium.q: Why did people from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon join Asa?

answers: People from other tribes who joined them
The priests serving at the altar
medium.explanation: The strangers included people from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who joined Asa's people.
medium.q: In this passage, who were the “strangers” gathered with Judah and Benjamin?

answers: He gathered the people, then removed idols, and finally took courage
He took courage, removed idols, renewed the altar, and gathered the people
He renewed the altar, went to war, and removed the people
challenge.explanation: The passage presents Asa taking courage, removing idols, renewing the altar, and gathering the people.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes Asa's response to the prophecy?

answers: They were impressed that the Lord was with him
They opposed the worship of the Lord
They wanted to take Judah away from Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The verse directly says they joined him when they saw that the Lord was with him.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from people of other tribes joining Asa?

answers: To gather before the Lord in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The people gathered together at Jerusalem in the third month of Asa's fifteenth year.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of the gathering in Jerusalem in Asa's fifteenth year?

paragraphs.title: The Covenant, the Oath, and the Joy

easy.explanation: They offered to the Lord from the spoil that they had brought.
easy.q: What did the people offer to the Lord?

easy.explanation: The passage says that they offered seven hundred oxen.
easy.q: How many oxen did they offer?

easy.explanation: All Judah rejoiced at the oath they had made to the Lord.
easy.q: What caused all Judah to rejoice?

answers: To seek the Lord with all their heart and soul
To enlarge the borders of the kingdom
medium.explanation: They entered into a covenant to seek the Lord with all their heart and soul.
medium.q: Why did the people enter into a covenant?

medium.explanation: They declared that anyone who would not seek the Lord should be put to death.
medium.q: What penalty did they accept for anyone who would not seek the Lord?

answers: With a loud voice, shouting, trumpets, and cornets
medium.explanation: They swore with a loud voice, with shouting, trumpets, and cornets.
medium.q: How did they swear unto the Lord?

answers: They sought Him wholeheartedly, and He gave them rest round about
They stopped worshipping the Lord, and therefore received rest
They went to war, so no enemies remained
challenge.explanation: The people sought the Lord with their whole desire, and the Lord gave them rest round about.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between seeking the Lord and receiving rest?

answers: The penalty applied only to the king
It applied to small and great, man and woman
Only the priests swore the oath
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically includes small and great, man and woman.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the covenant obligation included the whole people?

answers: They accepted the covenant willingly and wholeheartedly
They wanted to avoid all prayer
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes wholehearted commitment and sincere desire to seek the Lord.
challenge.q: What does seeking the Lord with their whole desire show about the people's oath?

paragraphs.title: Asa's Deeds, His Loyalty, and Peace in the Kingdom

easy.explanation: Asa removed Maachah, the mother of Asa the king, from being queen.
easy.q: Whom did Asa remove from being queen?

easy.explanation: The passage says that Maachah had made an idol in a grove.
easy.q: What had Maachah made in a grove?

answers: The fifteenth year of Asa's reign
The thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign
The seventieth year of Asa's reign
easy.explanation: There was no more war unto the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.
easy.q: Until what year was there no more war?

answers: He kept it in the royal house
He cut it down, stamped it, and burned it at the brook Kidron
medium.explanation: Asa cut down the idol, stamped it, and burned it at the brook Kidron.
medium.q: What did Asa do to Maachah's idol?

answers: The high places were not taken away
The altar of the Lord was destroyed
medium.explanation: The passage says that the high places were not taken away out of Israel.

answers: Dedicated things, silver, gold, and vessels
medium.explanation: Asa brought dedicated things, silver, gold, and vessels into the house of God.
medium.q: What did Asa bring into the house of God?

answers: He opposed idolatry even when it involved his own family
He abolished all worship of the Lord
He left every idol in its place
challenge.explanation: Asa removed his mother from being queen and destroyed the idol she had made.
challenge.q: What does Asa's removal of Maachah and her idol show?

answers: His heart was perfect, but the high places were not removed
The high places were removed, but his heart was not perfect
He had no dedicated things, but he had many wars
challenge.explanation: The passage says both that Asa's heart was perfect and that the high places remained.
challenge.q: What tension appears in the description of Asa's reign?

answers: Afterward there was no more war until Asa's thirty-fifth year
A great war began immediately afterward
Asa then abandoned the house of God
challenge.explanation: The chapter ends by stating that there was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.
challenge.q: How does the ending of the chapter relate to Asa's actions?
